body: We include `search-insights` here, but only `import type`, so doesn't affect bundle size.
The type didn't work with castToJestMock, and this new test should be the same.
Apparently, we have been using both `InsightsClient` and `InsightsClientWrapper`, but actually they were the same.
diff_hunk:

   InsightsClient,
   InsightsClientMethod,

body:
In this context we call only some methods that take one argument after `method`. However there are other methods like `onUserTokenChange` takes `(method, callback, options)`. So I had to put `...payloads` and use the first item.
Anyway `wrapInsightsClient` is deprecated, so I think it's fine.
For test, we've been using search-insights@v1, and now it uses v2 (which has more correct typings), so I had to explicitly put `useCookie: true` to keep the tests as-is.
This type is not used anywhere. Do we consider removing an exported type as a breaking change? If not, we can remove this.
is the contents really any and not the possible arguments to the function?

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4930/commits/84409a4a658be2d76fea9bb6a0a5bda5702d2c86

here's the change (thanks to you).

But thinking again, this `queue` is never going to be used by InstantSearch users. `queue` is written by the snippet of search-insights and read by itself and Insights middleware. I'm not sure who will get benefit from this typing, but it's good at least for the sake of correctness.
why not keep this a devDependency? only because of the types?

Would it be possible to move theses types in the search-insights ?
Any library using search-insights will need them IMHO, and it's hard to justify the fact that some of the types we use are baked-in and others like `QueueItem` are sitting here.
Actually `queue` is very internal, and normally no one uses it directly. Anyway, I think it's better to move it back to search-insights. I'll do it in the near future.
yes, the types are used in InstantSearch.js (it was used only in tests before)
